main_text.p: mano generi indultū beneficium, societatis scilicet vinculum; sic linguarum divisio horrendum erat irati Numinis judicium; societatis enim humanæ diffipatione minabatur: quod necessario eveniret, si tot essent linguæ quot homines, sic enim nec pater filium, nec maritus uxorem intelligere posset; quod ne eveniret, non singulis hominibus, sed singulis potius familiis peculiarem dialectum vel linguam Deum immisisse, quò in unam Coloniam melius coalescere possent, verisimile videtur. In hoc tamen summa emicuit Dei bonitas & providentia, (qui etiam ex malis bonum extrahere novit,) ut homines qui turrim Babylonicam construebant ne dispergerentur, linguarum divisione per omnes terras, quas filiis hominum colendas dedisset Deus, dispersi, earúmq; fructus ubique percipientes, gratâ linguarum harmoniâ Creatoris beneficentiam celebrarent; quód-que primò divinæ vindictæ signum erat, postea nascentis Ecclesiæ exordio, sic Deo volente, magnum esset amoris divini indicium: cùm qui primò linguarum varietatem in hominum animos immisit, ut dispergerentur; idem etiam linguarum donum inter alia χαρίσματα[?] Apostolis aliisque divinâ virtute contulit, ut Ecclesiam per orbem dispersam, palantésque Christi oves, in unum ovile colligerent, & pluribus linguis Τὰ μεγάλεια τῆς θεοῦ[?] prædicarent. Postquam enim Christus Dei filius, qui patris mandata Syro sermone Judæis exequutus fuerat, cœlos conscenderat, Spiritum Sanctum ad discipulos misit, eosque afflatu suo variarum linguarum peritissimos fecit; ut hisce cœlestis militiæ armis, quæ Turris Babylonicæ ædificatoribus ne cœlum ar-

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Several words were read at reduced clarity on the scan and are marked [?]: the Greek words in the line "inter alia" and "pluribus linguis", and the Greek word "χαρίσματα" which may be printed with different accents. The first line of the page continues from the previous page. The page ends mid-word with the printed hyphen "ar-". The catchword "rogantia" and signature "A 3" are the printed foot marks. Printed Greek is left in Greek letters as far as it could be read. A few Latin words near the top, such as "indultū" and "scilicet", are read from a faint scan and should be checked against the original.
